# Jan

Desktop app for local models. Turn on its local API server in settings.

| | |
|---|---|
| Kind | Chat API (OpenAI-compatible): returns code that conductor-ai applies |
| Cost | Free: runs on your machine. |
| Key | None (runs on your machine) |
| Endpoint | `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1` |
| Default model | picked automatically from the live list (coding models first); choose your own with `conductor-ai models jan --all` |
| conductor-ai name | `jan` |
| Provider docs | https://docs.jan.ai/desktop/api-server |
| Checked | 2026-11 |

## Set up

1. Install and start it: https://jan.ai. Turn on its local API server in settings.
2. Add it to conductor-ai. It asks for nothing, lets you pick a model, sends one test prompt and adds it to the `docs`, `test`, `review` and `ask` roles:
   ```bash
   conductor-ai add jan
   ```
3. Check it any time:
   ```bash
   conductor-ai doctor --live
   ```

Or click **Add** on its card in `conductor-ai ui` → Providers.

## Without the wizard

Then add this to `~/.config/conductor-ai/config.json` (all projects) or `.conductor-ai/config.json` (one project):
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "jan": {
      "type": "openai",
      "enabled": true,
      "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1",
      "apiKeyEnv": "",
      "model": "<model id>"
    }
  }
}
```
List models: `conductor-ai models jan --all`. Put `jan` in any role's chain in `conductor-ai ui` → Roles & fallback.

## Troubleshooting

- **401 / 403**: the key is wrong, expired, or still a placeholder. Run `conductor-ai keys` to see where it comes from.
- **404 or "model not found"**: the model id changed. Pick a current one with `conductor-ai models jan --all`.
- **429**: rate limit. conductor-ai puts the provider on cooldown and moves to the next one in the chain; `conductor-ai cooldown --clear jan` resets it.
- **Connection refused**: the local server isn't running at `http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1`.
- **Empty reply**: some free routes return nothing now and then; conductor-ai retries once, then falls back.
